Turtle Statue.name: Turtle Statue
Turtle Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when connected to wires and activated: Depending on the statue, upon activation it may spawn enemies , drop items , or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon , Underground Cabins , and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests . Like all furniture, a pickaxe , a drill , or explosives are used to collect them.

Amber Minecart.name: Amber Minecart
Amber Minecart.tooltip: Minecarts are mounts that allow players to ride on Minecart Tracks . When the player is near a Minecart Track, pressing the Quick Mount hotkey or pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on a point on the track causes a Minecart to spawn, which the player is automatically placed in. Once inside, the ▶ Right and ◀ Left direction keys either accelerate, decelerate, or reverse the cart's movement. The cart will maintain its current speed and direction if no keys are pressed and no obstacles are reached. The cart can also "jump" with the ↷ Jump key.

Bamboo.name: Bamboo
Bamboo.tooltip: Bamboo is a placeable block obtained by harvesting Bamboo stalks, which generate naturally in the Jungle biome, with any pickaxe or drill.

Bamboo Wall.name: Bamboo Wall
Bamboo Wall.tooltip: Bamboo Wall is a type of wall. As with most crafted walls, Bamboo Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.

Bamboo Bathtub.name: Bamboo Bathtub
Bamboo Bathtub.tooltip: The Bathtub is a decorative furniture item. It fulfills a house 's requirement of a flat-surface item .

Bamboo Bed.name: Bamboo Bed
Bamboo Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed. This requires it to be placed in a mostly valid house (see details below ). On the Desktop version , Console version , and Mobile version , Beds furthermore allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and gives a boost to health regeneration , similar to chairs and Sofas .

Bamboo Bookcase.name: Bamboo Bookcase
Bamboo Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons : the Crystal Storm , Cursed Flames , and Golden Shower . Bookcases also fulfill a house 's flat surface item requirement.

Bamboo Dresser.name: Bamboo Dresser
Bamboo Dresser.tooltip: Dressers are a type of furniture (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) as well as a storage item . It will also fulfill a house 's flat-surface item requirement.

Bamboo Candelabra.name: Bamboo Candelabra
Bamboo Candelabra.tooltip: Candelabras are a type of furniture and light source that emits light when placed on a flat surface such as blocks , platforms , and flat furniture items. It is not destroyed by water .

Bamboo Candle.name: Bamboo Candle
Bamboo Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source . Candles can be placed on Tables , Platforms , Crates or Work Benches . Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms .

Bamboo Chair.name: Bamboo Chair
Bamboo Chair.tooltip: The Chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on the ground. They count as a comfort item, which is one of the required elements in order to make a house suitable for an NPC . In combination with a Work Bench or a Table , they also form minor crafting stations.

Bamboo Chandelier.name: Bamboo Chandelier
Bamboo Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe , drill , or explosives . Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms .

Bamboo Chest.name: Bamboo Chest
Bamboo Chest.tooltip: Chests are storage items that each hold up to 40 item stacks in rows of 10×4 / 8×5. Chests can be broken with any pickaxe or drill , but only when empty. It is impossible to destroy the blocks underneath a placed Chest.

Bamboo Clock.name: Bamboo Clock
Bamboo Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time . If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap . The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches , but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner.

Bamboo Door.name: Bamboo Door
Bamboo Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that prevent enemies from entering an area when closed. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks . Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about.

Bamboo Lamp.name: Bamboo Lamp
Bamboo Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source . They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms . There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 37 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). All are functionally identical and differ only in their appearance.

Bamboo Lantern.name: Bamboo Lantern
Bamboo Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks ). They occupy less room than a chandelier , making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire .

Bamboo Piano.name: Bamboo Piano
Bamboo Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture . They also count as a flat surface item , which is one of the required elements in order to make a house .

Bamboo Platform.name: Bamboo Platform
Bamboo Platform.tooltip: Platforms are a special type of block that can be walked on, but also allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above.

Bamboo Sink.name: Bamboo Sink
Bamboo Sink.tooltip: The Sink is a type of furniture item and crafting station . It does not fulfill a house 's flat surface or comfort item requirement, however, it can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station.

Bamboo Sofa.name: Bamboo Sofa
Bamboo Sofa.tooltip: Sofas are vanity furniture items. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 38 / (Old-gen console version) 21 craftable sofas and 5 noncraftable sofas. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance. Sofas count as a comfort item, which is one of the required elements in order to make a house for an NPC .

Bamboo Table.name: Bamboo Table
Bamboo Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs . They count as a flat surface item , which is one of the required elements in order to make a house . They can also form a crafting station when combined with a chair.

Bamboo Work Bench.name: Bamboo Work Bench
Bamboo Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They are also one possible way to fulfill a house 's flat surface item requirement. Bottles , Pink Vases , and Mugs can be placed on it and used as a Placed Bottle for crafting potions . The Work Bench is the first crafting station the player can make in the game, and one of the first items overall.

Trapped Bamboo Chest.name: Trapped Bamboo Chest
Trapped Bamboo Chest.tooltip: A Trapped Chest is a mechanical item that has the appearance of a normal chest . It cannot be used for storage , as it does not have any storage slots. When it is opened, it emits a signal and can be connected with wire .

Bamboo Toilet.name: Bamboo Toilet
Bamboo Toilet.tooltip: Toilets are furniture items which can be placed on the ground. They are functionally similar to chairs , and count as comfort items for NPC house requirements. In combination with a Work Bench or a Table , they also form minor crafting stations. Only the Toilet and Golden Toilet are considered as a valid crafting station .

Music Box (Jungle Night).name: Music Box (Jungle Night)

Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Bamboo Fence.name: Bamboo Fence
Bamboo Fence.tooltip: Fences are a type of safe wall that are visually thin with most of them having transparency to allow view of the background. The only fences that have no transparency to them are Palm Fence , Rich Mahogany Fence , and Shadewood Fence . Unlike most other safe walls , they allow for wild plants and trees , except for palm trees and its variants, to grow. The safe grass wall , flower wall , and jungle wall are functionally identical to fences.

Illuminant Coating.name: Illuminant Coating
Illuminant Coating.tooltip: Paint is used to modify the color of objects. Nearly anything can be painted, including blocks , background walls , and furniture , along with non-collectable environment objects like trees , tall grass, flowers, and other ambient growth. Basic paint is purchased from the Painter NPC . Two of the same color can be combined at a Dye Vat to create "deep" color versions, which apply their color more vividly and are required in order to paint certain objects.

Desert Chest.name: Desert Chest
Desert Chest.tooltip: Biome Chests are Hardmode Chests found within the Dungeon . Each contains one specific rare, powerful weapon, in addition to other miscellaneous items. While Biome Chests are placed during world creation, they are initially locked and can only be opened with an appropriate Biome Key , which will only become available in Hardmode.

Trapped Desert Chest.name: Trapped Desert Chest
Trapped Desert Chest.tooltip: A Trapped Chest is a mechanical item that has the appearance of a normal chest . It cannot be used for storage , as it does not have any storage slots. When it is opened, it emits a signal and can be connected with wire .

Desert Key.name: Desert Key
Desert Key.tooltip: Biome Keys are Hardmode items used to open the Biome Chests in the Dungeon . Opening a Chest consumes the key. Though unusable until Plantera is defeated, they can be dropped at any time during Hardmode. Each key has a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance of dropping from an enemy in the key's respective biome .

Stellar Tune.name: Stellar Tune
Stellar Tune.tooltip: The Stellar Tune is a Hardmode, post-Plantera magic weapon that fires pairs of star-shaped projectiles that travel in a wave-like pattern toward the cursor and home in on enemies, travel through solid blocks, and explode in a small radius upon impact.

Ghostar's Infinity Eight.name: Ghostar's Infinity Eight
Ghostar's Infinity Eight.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly temporarily by holding the ↷ Jump button. They also provide immunity to fall damage . After flight time has run out, holding the ↷ Jump button allows the player to glide, slowing falling speed. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes ), or hooks onto a block. Flight is much more controlled with wings than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time.

Terra Toilet.name: Terra Toilet
Terra Toilet.tooltip: Toilets are furniture items which can be placed on the ground. They are functionally similar to chairs , and count as comfort items for NPC house requirements. In combination with a Work Bench or a Table , they also form minor crafting stations. Only the Toilet and Golden Toilet are considered as a valid crafting station .

Coffin Minecart.name: Coffin Minecart
Coffin Minecart.tooltip: Minecarts are mounts that allow players to ride on Minecart Tracks . When the player is near a Minecart Track, pressing the Quick Mount hotkey or pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on a point on the track causes a Minecart to spawn, which the player is automatically placed in. Once inside, the ▶ Right and ◀ Left direction keys either accelerate, decelerate, or reverse the cart's movement. The cart will maintain its current speed and direction if no keys are pressed and no obstacles are reached. The cart can also "jump" with the ↷ Jump key.

Grox The Great's Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly temporarily by holding the ↷ Jump button. They also provide immunity to fall damage . After flight time has run out, holding the ↷ Jump button allows the player to glide, slowing falling speed. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes ), or hooks onto a block. Flight is much more controlled with wings than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time.

Grox The Great's Horned Cowl.name: Grox The Great's Horned Cowl
Grox The Great's Horned Cowl.tooltip: Grox The Great's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime 's). It is the vanity set made for Grox The Great , one of the programmers who develops Terraria .

Grox The Great's Chestplate.name: Grox The Great's Chestplate
Grox The Great's Chestplate.tooltip: Grox The Great's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime 's). It is the vanity set made for Grox The Great , one of the programmers who develops Terraria .

Grox The Great's Greaves.name: Grox The Great's Greaves
Grox The Great's Greaves.tooltip: Grox The Great's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime 's). It is the vanity set made for Grox The Great , one of the programmers who develops Terraria .

Blade Staff.name: Blade Staff
Blade Staff.tooltip: The Blade Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons an Enchanted Dagger minion.

Squirrel Hook.name: Squirrel Hook
Squirrel Hook.tooltip: The Squirrel Hook is a pre-Hardmode grappling hook that fires a single hook that reaches 19 tiles, and functions identically to a normal grappling hook but has the unique ability to grapple and attach to the trunks of trees and Giant Glowing Mushrooms.

Sergeant United Shield.name: Sergeant United Shield
Sergeant United Shield.tooltip: The Sergeant United Shield is a Hardmode boomerang that is rarely sold by the Traveling Merchant for 35 GC.

Rock Golem Head.name: Rock Golem Head
Rock Golem Head.tooltip: The Rock Golem Head is a dual-purpose vanity and furniture item dropped by Rock Golems at a 1/10 (10%) chance.

Critter Shampoo.name: Critter Shampoo
Critter Shampoo.tooltip: Critter Shampoo is a vanity accessory equipped in a social accessory slot that changes the color of summoned minions when paired with a dye in the corresponding dye slot.

Digging Molecart.name: Digging Molecart
Digging Molecart.tooltip: The Digging Molecart is a minecart that automatically digs a tunnel and lays down regular Minecart Tracks.

Shroomerang.name: Shroomerang
Shroomerang.tooltip: The Shroomerang is a pre-Hardmode boomerang that is dropped by Spore Bats with a 1/40 (2.5%) chance.

Tree Globe.name: Tree Globe
Tree Globe.tooltip: The Tree Globe is a thrown consumable item sold by the Zoologist for 3 GC after 50% of the Bestiary (270 entries) has been filled out.

World Globe.name: World Globe
World Globe.tooltip: The World Globe is a thrown consumable item sold by the Zoologist after the Bestiary is 50% complete (270 entries).

Guide to Critter Companionship.name: Guide to Critter Companionship
Guide to Critter Companionship.tooltip: The Guide to Critter Companionship is a pre-Hardmode tool that prevents the player's attacks from harming critters while inside their inventory.

Dog Ears.name: Dog Ears
Dog Ears.tooltip: The Dog set is a vanity set composed of the Dog Tail and Dog Ears . It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a Full Moon or a Waning Gibbous for 6 GC (set) .

Dog Tail.name: Dog Tail
Dog Tail.tooltip: The Dog set is a vanity set composed of the Dog Tail and Dog Ears . It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a Full Moon or a Waning Gibbous for 6 GC (set) .

Fox Ears.name: Fox Ears

Fox Tail.name: Fox Tail

Lizard Ears.name: Lizard Ears
Lizard Ears.tooltip: The Lizard set is a vanity set composed of the Lizard Tail and the Lizard Ears . It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a New Moon or a Waxing Crescent for 6 GC (set) .

Lizard Tail.name: Lizard Tail
Lizard Tail.tooltip: The Lizard set is a vanity set composed of the Lizard Tail and the Lizard Ears . It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a New Moon or a Waxing Crescent for 6 GC (set) .

Panda Ears.name: Panda Ears
Panda Ears.tooltip: Panda Ears are a vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 GC50 SC.

Bunny Tail.name: Bunny Tail
Bunny Tail.tooltip: The Bunny set is a vanity set composed of the Bunny Tail and Bunny Ears . It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a First Quarter or a Waxing Gibbous for 6 GC (set) .

Fairy Glowstick.name: Fairy Glowstick
Fairy Glowstick.tooltip: The Fairy Glowstick is a consumable light source sold by the Zoologist for 75 CC when all three fairies have been recorded in the Bestiary.

Lightning Carrot.name: Lightning Carrot
Lightning Carrot.tooltip: The Lightning Carrot is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Volt Bunny that follows the player.

Prismatic Dye.name: Prismatic Dye
Prismatic Dye.tooltip: Prismatic Dye is a Hardmode, post-Plantera dye dropped by the Empress of Light with a 1/4 (25%) chance.
Prismatic Dye.drops_summary: Empress of Light (25%), Treasure Bag (Empress of Light) (25%)

Mushroom Hat.name: Mushroom Hat
Mushroom Hat.tooltip: The Mushroom set is a vanity set consisting of the Mushroom Hat , Mushroom Vest , and Mushroom Pants . All three pieces have a 1/2 (50%) chance of being found in Mushroom Chests in underground Glowing Mushroom biomes .

Mushroom Vest.name: Mushroom Vest
Mushroom Vest.tooltip: The Mushroom set is a vanity set consisting of the Mushroom Hat , Mushroom Vest , and Mushroom Pants . All three pieces have a 1/2 (50%) chance of being found in Mushroom Chests in underground Glowing Mushroom biomes .

Mushroom Pants.name: Mushroom Pants
Mushroom Pants.tooltip: The Mushroom set is a vanity set consisting of the Mushroom Hat , Mushroom Vest , and Mushroom Pants . All three pieces have a 1/2 (50%) chance of being found in Mushroom Chests in underground Glowing Mushroom biomes .

Treasure Bag (Empress of Light).name: Treasure Bag (Empress of Light)
Treasure Bag (Empress of Light).tooltip: Treasure Bags are consumable grab bag -like items obtained in Expert Mode and Master Mode as a reward for defeating bosses . The contents and appearance of Treasure Bags depend on the boss it comes from, and are opened by using either ⚷ Open / Activate while inside the inventory , or ⚒ Use / Attack when selected in the hotbar . In multiplayer , each player that deals damage to the boss receives one Treasure Bag upon defeating it. Treasure Bags are client-side and will despawn upon exiting the world. See Notes for details.

Empress of Light Trophy.name: Empress of Light Trophy
Empress of Light Trophy.tooltip: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses . While they can be considered the "boss version of banners ", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests . In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Empress of Light Mask.name: Empress of Light Mask
Empress of Light Mask.tooltip: Masks are vanity items dropped by all non- event bosses , as well as those from the Old One's Army (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) . They are worn in the social head slot.

Dusty Rawhide Saddle.name: Dusty Rawhide Saddle
Dusty Rawhide Saddle.tooltip: The Dusty Rawhide Saddle , Royal Gilded Saddle , and Black Studded Saddle are mount-summoning items that summon the rideable Painted Horse Mount , Majestic Horse Mount , and Dark Horse Mount , respectively. All three horse mounts are functionally identical. Once they reach a high speed, they will deal damage to enemies they come into contact with. Saddles are sold by the Zoologist for 25 GC each, after completing at least 30% (162 entries) of the Bestiary .

Royal Gilded Saddle.tooltip: The Dusty Rawhide Saddle , Royal Gilded Saddle , and Black Studded Saddle are mount-summoning items that summon the rideable Painted Horse Mount , Majestic Horse Mount , and Dark Horse Mount , respectively. All three horse mounts are functionally identical. Once they reach a high speed, they will deal damage to enemies they come into contact with. Toy Tank.name: Toy Tank

Goat Skull.name: Goat Skull

Royal Delight.name: Royal Delight

Suspicious Grinning Eye.name: Suspicious Grinning Eye

Pair of Eyeballs.name: Pair of Eyeballs

Bottomless Lava Bucket.name: Bottomless Lava Bucket
Bottomless Lava Bucket.tooltip: Bottomless Buckets are tools that are capable of placing an infinite amount of liquids by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button. Lavaproof Bug Net.name: Lavaproof Bug Net
Lavaproof Bug Net.tooltip: The Lavaproof Bug Net is an upgraded version of the Bug Net.

Flame Waker Boots.name: Flame Waker Boots
Flame Waker Boots.tooltip: The Flame Waker Boots are a vanity accessory obtained by opening Obsidian Crates or Hellstone Crates, found by fishing in Lava.

Wet Bomb.tooltip: Liquid bombs are explosive items which either place or remove liquids instead of solid blocks when exploding. There are four different types of liquid bombs: Dry Bomb , Wet Bomb , Lava Bomb , and Honey Bomb .

Hell Butterfly.name: Hell Butterfly
Hell Butterfly.tooltip: Butterflies are small critters that can be found in Forests during daytime . They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest or Pearlwood tree during the day. They can be caught with a Bug Net (except for the Hell Butterfly (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) ) and carried in the inventory or crafted into butterfly jars . They can also be used as bait for fishing .

Hell Butterfly Jar.name: Hell Butterfly Jar
Hell Butterfly Jar.tooltip: Butterfly jars are pieces of decorative furniture created by combining a butterfly , captured with a Bug Net , with a Bottle . By throwing a butterfly jar into shimmer , it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the butterfly as an item.

Lavafly.name: Lavafly
Lavafly.tooltip: The Lavafly is a critter that spawns occasionally in the Underworld at night.

Lavafly in a Bottle.name: Lavafly in a Bottle
Lavafly in a Bottle.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks ). They occupy less room than a chandelier , making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire .

Magma Snail.name: Magma Snail
Magma Snail.tooltip: The Magma Snail is a critter that spawns in The Underworld.

Magma Snail Cage.name: Magma Snail Cage
Magma Snail Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters . A critter caught with the Bug Net , Lavaproof Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) , or Golden Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into shimmer , it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item.

Topaz Gemcorn.name: Topaz Gemcorn
Topaz Gemcorn.tooltip: Gemcorns are seeds crafted from an Acorn and any gem . When placed, they create saplings that can grow into gem trees . Natural gem trees occasionally generate within the Underground and Cavern layers. Destroying a gem tree generally yields 7–48 Stone Blocks , 0–11 Gemcorns of the tree's type, and 0–24 gems of the tree's type (each tile of the tree has a 1/10 (10%) chance of dropping a gem, otherwise dropping 1–2 Stone Blocks, and every non-barren leaf/branch tile additionally has a 1/2 (50%) chance to drop another Gemcorn [ 1 ] . See Growing conditions section for detailed info ).

Lava Absorbant Sponge.name: Lava Absorbant Sponge
Lava Absorbant Sponge.tooltip: Sponges are tools used to erase liquids by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on them. This causes the liquid to disappear from the environment without storing it. There are four different types of sponges:

Hallowed Hood.name: Hallowed Hood
Hallowed Hood.tooltip: Hallowed armor is a Hardmode , post- mechanical boss armor set consisting of the Hallowed Plate Mail and Hallowed Greaves , as well as four different headpieces: the Hallowed Mask , Hallowed Helmet , Hallowed Headgear , and Hallowed Hood , providing bonuses for melee, ranged, magic, and summon damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Hallowed Bars . Crafting all six pieces requires a total of 90 Hallowed Bars.

Hellfire Treads.name: Hellfire Treads
Hellfire Treads.tooltip: The Hellfire Treads are a pre-Hardmode accessory that combines the effects of the Spectre and Flame Waker Boots.

Jungle Pylon.name: Jungle Pylon

Obsidian Lock Box.name: Obsidian Lock Box

Lava Serpent Bowl.name: Lava Serpent Bowl
Lava Serpent Bowl.tooltip: The Fish Bowl , Gold Fish Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) , Pupfish Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) , and Lava Serpent Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are decorative furniture items. The Fish Bowl and Gold Fish Bowl also double as wearable items that can be equipped in the player's helmet slot.

Lavaproof Fishing Hook.name: Lavaproof Fishing Hook

Ancient Hallowed Mask.name: Ancient Hallowed Mask
Ancient Hallowed Mask.tooltip: Ancient Hallowed armor is a Hardmode armor set. It has ranged, melee, summoner, and magic set versions, depending on the equipped headpiece. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires 54 Hallowed Bars (dropped by the mechanical bosses ), or 90 Hallowed Bars for the full set including all four headpieces. Wearing a full set gives off a faint pulsing aura around the player and displays an after-image effect while in motion. To acquire the necessary Hallowed Bars for a full set with one helmet, a player will need to kill a mechanical boss 2-4 times, and 3-4 times for all four helmets.

Cavern Water Fountain.name: Cavern Water Fountain

There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 10 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 8 different obtainable fountains, all of which are purchased from the Witch Doctor for 4 GC each at any time. On the Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS versions , they are able to be purchased for free, but are only available after Plantera has been defeated. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The range of a Fountain is (when measured from the edges of the sprite) 60 tiles left, 53 tiles up, 60 tiles right, and 53 tiles down.

Treasure Bag (Queen Slime).name: Treasure Bag (Queen Slime)
Treasure Bag (Queen Slime).tooltip: Treasure Bags are consumable grab bag -like items obtained in Expert Mode and Master Mode as a reward for defeating bosses . The contents and appearance of Treasure Bags depend on the boss it comes from, and are opened by using either ⚷ Open / Activate while inside the inventory , or ⚒ Use / Attack when selected in the hotbar . In multiplayer , each player that deals damage to the boss receives one Treasure Bag upon defeating it. Treasure Bags are client-side and will despawn upon exiting the world. See Notes for details.

Queen Slime Trophy.name: Queen Slime Trophy
Queen Slime Trophy.tooltip: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses . While they can be considered the "boss version of banners ", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests . In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Queen Slime Mask.name: Queen Slime Mask
Queen Slime Mask.tooltip: Masks are vanity items dropped by all non- event bosses , as well as those from the Old One's Army (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) . They are worn in the social head slot.

Regal Delicacy.name: Regal Delicacy
Regal Delicacy.tooltip: The Regal Delicacy is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Slime Princess that follows the player.

Prismatic Lacewing.name: Prismatic Lacewing
Prismatic Lacewing.tooltip: The Prismatic Lacewing is a rare Hardmode, post-Plantera flying critter and boss-summoning item that spawns on the surface Hallow after Plantera has been defeated.

Stone Accent Slab.name: Stone Accent Slab
Stone Accent Slab.tooltip: The Stone Accent Slab is a block which is visually identical to the Stone Slab, except that it does not blend with any blocks other than itself and Smooth Marble Blocks.

Truffle Worm Cage.name: Truffle Worm Cage
Truffle Worm Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters . A critter caught with the Bug Net , Lavaproof Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) , or Golden Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into shimmer , it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item.

Prismatic Lacewing Jar.name: Prismatic Lacewing Jar
Prismatic Lacewing Jar.tooltip: The Prismatic Lacewing Jar is a placeable furniture item which displays the Prismatic Lacewing, normally a critter which summons the Empress of Light boss if killed.

Rock Golem Banner.name: Rock Golem Banner
Rock Golem Banner.tooltip: Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks and platforms . They are dropped by most enemies and a few critters .

Music Box (Queen Slime).name: Music Box (Queen Slime)
Music Box (Queen Slime).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 GC . When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

Hook of Dissonance.name: Hook of Dissonance
Hook of Dissonance.tooltip: The Hook of Dissonance is a Hardmode grappling hook that fires a single hook that reaches 30 tiles; when the hook attaches to a block, it will instantly teleport the user to the hook's position if the path to the hook is wide enough to fit a player.

Gelatinous Pillion.name: Gelatinous Pillion
Gelatinous Pillion.tooltip: The Gelatinous Pillion is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a friendly Winged Slime Mount.

Crystal Assassin Hood.name: Crystal Assassin Hood
Crystal Assassin Hood.tooltip: Crystal Assassin armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Crystal Assassin Hood , Crystal Assassin Shirt , and Crystal Assassin Pants . Queen Slime always drops one piece / two pieces upon defeat.

Crystal Assassin Shirt.name: Crystal Assassin Shirt

Badger's Hat.name: Badger's Hat

When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

Deerclops Trophy.name: Deerclops Trophy
Deerclops Trophy.tooltip: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses . While they can be considered the "boss version of banners ", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests . In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Deerclops Mask.name: Deerclops Mask

Deerclops Relic.name: Deerclops Relic
Deerclops Relic.tooltip: Relics are furniture items dropped by bosses and mini-bosses in Master Mode . They are golden depictions of their respective boss that hover above a pedestal, have a golden particle effect, and emit light when placed close to a light source .

Treasure Bag (Deerclops).name: Treasure Bag (Deerclops)
Treasure Bag (Deerclops).tooltip: Treasure Bags are consumable grab bag -like items obtained in Expert Mode and Master Mode as a reward for defeating bosses . The contents and appearance of Treasure Bags depend on the boss it comes from, and are opened by using either ⚷ Open / Activate while inside the inventory , or ⚒ Use / Attack when selected in the hotbar . In multiplayer , each player that deals damage to the boss receives one Treasure Bag upon defeating it. Treasure Bags are client-side and will despawn upon exiting the world. See Notes for details.

Fart Kart.name: Fart Kart
Fart Kart.tooltip: Minecarts are mounts that allow players to ride on Minecart Tracks . When the player is near a Minecart Track, pressing the Quick Mount hotkey or pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on a point on the track causes a Minecart to spawn, which the player is automatically placed in. Once inside, the ▶ Right and ◀ Left direction keys either accelerate, decelerate, or reverse the cart's movement. The cart will maintain its current speed and direction if no keys are pressed and no obstacles are reached. The cart can also "jump" with the ↷ Jump key.

Moss sprouts fuzz that can be cut like grass weeds.

By throwing a cage into shimmer , it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item.

Terraformer.name: Terraformer
Terraformer.tooltip: The Terraformer is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord tool.

Venom Dart Trap.name: Venom Dart Trap
Venom Dart Trap.tooltip: The Venom Dart Trap is a Hardmode trap that fires a venomous dart when triggered via wire.

Vulkelf Ears.name: Vulkelf Ears
Vulkelf Ears.tooltip: Vulkelf Ears are a vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 GC50 SC.

Stinkbug Blocker.name: Stinkbug Blocker
Stinkbug Blocker.tooltip: The Stinkbug Blocker and Ghostly Stinkbug Blocker are furniture items.

Ghostly Stinkbug Blocker.name: Ghostly Stinkbug Blocker
Ghostly Stinkbug Blocker.tooltip: The Stinkbug Blocker and Ghostly Stinkbug Blocker are furniture items. When placed in a valid house , they will prevent NPCs from moving in.

Fishing Bobber.name: Fishing Bobber
Fishing Bobber.tooltip: Fishing Bobbers are accessories that change the appearance of a fishing pole's bobber and increase the player's Fishing Power by 10.

Glowing Fishing Bobber.name: Glowing Fishing Bobber
Glowing Fishing Bobber.tooltip: Fishing Bobbers are accessories that change the appearance of a fishing pole 's bobber and increase the player's Fishing Power by 10.

Lava Moss Fishing Bobber.name: Lava Moss Fishing Bobber
Lava Moss Fishing Bobber.tooltip: Fishing Bobbers are accessories that change the appearance of a fishing pole 's bobber and increase the player's Fishing Power by 10.

Wand of Frosting.name: Wand of Frosting
Wand of Frosting.tooltip: The Wand of Frosting is a pre-Hardmode wand and the direct upgrade to the Wand of Sparking.

Reef Bathtub.name: Reef Bathtub
Reef Bathtub.tooltip: The Bathtub is a decorative furniture item. It fulfills a house 's requirement of a flat-surface item .

Reef Bed.name: Reef Bed
Reef Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed. This requires it to be placed in a mostly valid house (see details below ). On the Desktop version , Console version , and Mobile version , Beds furthermore allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and gives a boost to health regeneration , similar to chairs and Sofas .

Reef Bookcase.name: Reef Bookcase
Reef Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons : the Crystal Storm , Cursed Flames , and Golden Shower . Bookcases also fulfill a house 's flat surface item requirement.

Reef Dresser.name: Reef Dresser
Reef Dresser.tooltip: Dressers are a type of furniture (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) as well as a storage item . It will also fulfill a house 's flat-surface item requirement.

Reef Candelabra.name: Reef Candelabra
Reef Candelabra.tooltip: Candelabras are a type of furniture and light source that emits light when placed on a flat surface such as blocks , platforms , and flat furniture items. It is not destroyed by water .

Reef Candle.name: Reef Candle
Reef Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source . Candles can be placed on Tables , Platforms , Crates or Work Benches . Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms .

Reef Chair.name: Reef Chair
Reef Chair.tooltip: The Chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on the ground. They count as a comfort item, which is one of the required elements in order to make a house suitable for an NPC . In combination with a Work Bench or a Table , they also form minor crafting stations.

Reef Chandelier.name: Reef Chandelier
Reef Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe , drill , or explosives . Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms .

Reef Chest.name: Reef Chest
Reef Chest.tooltip: Chests are storage items that each hold up to 40 item stacks in rows of 10×4 / 8×5. Chests can be broken with any pickaxe or drill , but only when empty. It is impossible to destroy the blocks underneath a placed Chest.

Reef Clock.name: Reef Clock
Reef Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time . If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap . The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches , but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner.

Reef Door.name: Reef Door
Reef Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that prevent enemies from entering an area when closed. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks . Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about.

Reef Lamp.name: Reef Lamp
Reef Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source . They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms . There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 37 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). All are functionally identical and differ only in their appearance.

Reef Lantern.name: Reef Lantern
Reef Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks ). They occupy less room than a chandelier , making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire .

Reef Piano.name: Reef Piano
Reef Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture . They also count as a flat surface item , which is one of the required elements in order to make a house .

Reef Platform.name: Reef Platform
Reef Platform.tooltip: Platforms are a special type of block that can be walked on, but also allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above.

Reef Sink.name: Reef Sink
Reef Sink.tooltip: The Sink is a type of furniture item and crafting station . It does not fulfill a house 's flat surface or comfort item requirement, however, it can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station.

Reef Sofa.name: Reef Sofa
Reef Sofa.tooltip: Sofas are vanity furniture items. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 38 / (Old-gen console version) 21 craftable sofas and 5 noncraftable sofas. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance. Sofas count as a comfort item, which is one of the required elements in order to make a house for an NPC .

Reef Table.name: Reef Table
Reef Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs . They count as a flat surface item , which is one of the required elements in order to make a house . They can also form a crafting station when combined with a chair.

Reef Work Bench.name: Reef Work Bench
Reef Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They are also one possible way to fulfill a house 's flat surface item requirement. Bottles , Pink Vases , and Mugs can be placed on it and used as a Placed Bottle for crafting potions . The Work Bench is the first crafting station the player can make in the game, and one of the first items overall.

Trapped Reef Chest.name: Trapped Reef Chest
Trapped Reef Chest.tooltip: A Trapped Chest is a mechanical item that has the appearance of a normal chest . It cannot be used for storage , as it does not have any storage slots. When it is opened, it emits a signal and can be connected with wire .

Reef Toilet.name: Reef Toilet
Reef Toilet.tooltip: Toilets are furniture items which can be placed on the ground. They are functionally similar to chairs , and count as comfort items for NPC house requirements. In combination with a Work Bench or a Table , they also form minor crafting stations. Only the Toilet and Golden Toilet are considered as a valid crafting station .

Biome Sight Potion.name: Biome Sight Potion
Biome Sight Potion.tooltip: The Biome Sight Potion is a buff potion which grants the Biome Sight buff when consumed.

Scarlet Macaw.name: Scarlet Macaw
Scarlet Macaw.tooltip: The Scarlet Macaw and Blue Macaw are critters that spawn in the Jungle during the daytime . They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Mahogany tree during the day.

Scarlet Macaw Cage.name: Scarlet Macaw Cage
Scarlet Macaw Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters . A critter caught with the Bug Net , Lavaproof Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) , or Golden Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. Ash Grass Seeds.name: Ash Grass Seeds
Ash Grass Seeds.tooltip: Ash Grass Seeds are seeds used to plant Ash grass.

Ash Wood.name: Ash Wood
Ash Wood.tooltip: Ash Wood is a type of wood harvested from Ash trees found naturally growing in Ash forests.

Ash Wood Wall.name: Ash Wood Wall
Ash Wood Wall.tooltip: Ash Wood Wall is a type of background wall crafted using Ash Wood.

Ash Wood Fence.name: Ash Wood Fence
Ash Wood Fence.tooltip: Fences are a type of safe wall that are visually thin with most of them having transparency to allow view of the background. The only fences that have no transparency to them are Palm Fence , Rich Mahogany Fence , and Shadewood Fence . Unlike most other safe walls , they allow for wild plants and trees , except for palm trees and its variants, to grow. The safe grass wall , flower wall , and jungle wall are functionally identical to fences.

Outcast.name: Outcast
Outcast.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls . Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria -related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members ( see Trivia below ) . (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions , the Magic Lantern , Spelunker Glowsticks , and Spelunker Flares .

Terra Fart Kart.name: Terra Fart Kart
Terra Fart Kart.tooltip: Minecarts are mounts that allow players to ride on Minecart Tracks . When the player is near a Minecart Track, pressing the Quick Mount hotkey or pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on a point on the track causes a Minecart to spawn, which the player is automatically placed in. Once inside, the ▶ Right and ◀ Left direction keys either accelerate, decelerate, or reverse the cart's movement. The cart will maintain its current speed and direction if no keys are pressed and no obstacles are reached. The cart can also "jump" with the ↷ Jump key.

Minecart Upgrade Kit.name: Minecart Upgrade Kit
Minecart Upgrade Kit.tooltip: The Minecart Upgrade Kit is a Hardmode permanent booster item that permanently unlocks a boost for all Minecarts, including a speed increase, extra defense when moving, and a laser attack.

Jim's Cap.name: Jim's Cap
Jim's Cap.tooltip: Jim's Cap is an vanity item. It will always drop from the Painter, but only when his name is Jim.

Echo Wall.name: Echo Wall
Echo Wall.tooltip: The Echo Wall is a type of background wall made from Echo Blocks.

Echo Platform.name: Echo Platform
Echo Platform.tooltip: Platforms are a special type of block that can be walked on, but also allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above.

Mushroom Torch.name: Mushroom Torch
Mushroom Torch.tooltip: Torches are furniture items that produce light when placed , held, or dropped (via the Throw key), and are crucial at all stages of gameplay as primary light sources . Torches provide light permanently, and are never extinguished. Regular Torches can be found randomly in Chests and Pots , as a bonus drop from slimes , or purchased from the Merchant or Skeleton Merchant for 50 CC each.

Hive-Five.name: Hive-Five
Hive-Five.tooltip: The Hive-Five is a pre-Hardmode yoyo. Upon enemy hits, it has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of summoning a homing Bee projectile.

Axe of Regrowth.name: Axe of Regrowth
Axe of Regrowth.tooltip: The Axe of Regrowth is a pre-Hardmode tool that has the functionalities of the Staff of Regrowth along with the ability to function as an axe and automatically plant Acorns when trees are chopped.

Chlorophyte Extractinator.name: Chlorophyte Extractinator
Chlorophyte Extractinator.tooltip: The Chlorophyte Extractinator is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses crafting station and the upgrade to the Extractinator.

Blue Chicken Egg.name: Blue Chicken Egg
Blue Chicken Egg.tooltip: The Blue Chicken Egg is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Blue Chicken that follows the player.

Trimarang.name: Trimarang
Trimarang.tooltip: The Trimarang is a pre-Hardmode boomerang crafted using three different boomerangs.

Mushroom Campfire.name: Mushroom Campfire
Mushroom Campfire.tooltip: The Campfire is a placed furniture item that emits light and provides the Cozy Fire buff to players in its vicinity. A Campfire can be turned off by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on the object or by sending it a wire signal, and can be toggled back on again the same way. It is also used to cook a Marshmallow on a Stick .

Blue Macaw.name: Blue Macaw
Blue Macaw.tooltip: The Scarlet Macaw and Blue Macaw are critters that spawn in the Jungle during the daytime . They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Mahogany tree during the day.

Blue Macaw Cage.name: Blue Macaw Cage
Blue Macaw Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters . A critter caught with the Bug Net , Lavaproof Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) , or Golden Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into shimmer , it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item.

Bottomless Honey Bucket.name: Bottomless Honey Bucket
Bottomless Honey Bucket.tooltip: Bottomless Buckets are tools that are capable of placing an infinite amount of liquids by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button. There are four different types of Bottomless Buckets, one for each type of liquid: Bottomless Water Bucket , Bottomless Lava Bucket , Bottomless Honey Bucket , and Bottomless Shimmer Bucket .

Honey Absorbant Sponge.name: Honey Absorbant Sponge
Honey Absorbant Sponge.tooltip: Sponges are tools used to erase liquids by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on them. This causes the liquid to disappear from the environment without storing it. There are four different types of sponges:

Ultra Absorbant Sponge.name: Ultra Absorbant Sponge
Ultra Absorbant Sponge.tooltip: Sponges are tools used to erase liquids by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on them. This causes the liquid to disappear from the environment without storing it. There are four different types of sponges:

Goblorc Ears.name: Goblorc Ears
Goblorc Ears.tooltip: The Goblorc Ears are a vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 GC50 SC.

Reef Block.name: Reef Block
Reef Block.tooltip: Reef Blocks are a type of decorative block. They can be used to craft Reef furniture.

Reef Wall.name: Reef Wall
Reef Wall.tooltip: Reef Walls are a type of background wall. They are crafted with Reef Blocks at a Work Bench.

r/Terraria.name: r/Terraria
r/Terraria.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls . Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria -related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members ( see Trivia below ) . (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions , the Magic Lantern , Spelunker Glowsticks , and Spelunker Flares .

Guide to Environmental Preservation.name: Guide to Environmental Preservation
Guide to Environmental Preservation.tooltip: The Guide to Environmental Preservation is a pre-Hardmode tool that prevents the player's attacks from breaking plants while inside their inventory.

Princess Style.name: Princess Style
Princess Style.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls . Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria -related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members ( see Trivia below ) . (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions , the Magic Lantern , Spelunker Glowsticks , and Spelunker Flares .

Toucan.name: Toucan
Toucan.tooltip: The Toucan is a critter that spawns in the Jungle during the daytime.

Yellow Cockatiel.name: Yellow Cockatiel
Yellow Cockatiel.tooltip: The Yellow Cockatiel and Gray Cockatiel are critters that spawn in the Jungle during the daytime . They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Mahogany tree during the day.

Gray Cockatiel.name: Gray Cockatiel
Gray Cockatiel.tooltip: The Yellow Cockatiel and Gray Cockatiel are critters that spawn in the Jungle during the daytime . They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Mahogany tree during the day.

Toucan Cage.name: Toucan Cage
Toucan Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters . A critter caught with the Bug Net , Lavaproof Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) , or Golden Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into shimmer , it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item.

Yellow Cockatiel Cage.name: Yellow Cockatiel Cage
Yellow Cockatiel Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters . Macaw Statue.name: Macaw Statue
Macaw Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when connected to wires and activated: Depending on the statue, upon activation it may spawn enemies , drop items , or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon , Underground Cabins , and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests . Like all furniture, a pickaxe , a drill , or explosives are used to collect them.

Toucan Statue.name: Toucan Statue
Toucan Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when connected to wires and activated: Depending on the statue, upon activation it may spawn enemies , drop items , or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon , Underground Cabins , and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests . Like all furniture, a pickaxe , a drill , or explosives are used to collect them.

Cockatiel Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. Decorative Healing Potion.name: Decorative Healing Potion
Decorative Healing Potion.tooltip: The Decorative Healing Potion is a furniture item.

Decorative Mana Potion.name: Decorative Mana Potion
Decorative Mana Potion.tooltip: The Decorative Mana Potion is a furniture item. By pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button or mining it, it drops a Lesser Mana Potion.

Shadow Candle.name: Shadow Candle
Shadow Candle.tooltip: The Shadow Candle is a furniture item that can be placed or held to nullify the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area.

Guide to Peaceful Coexistence.name: Guide to Peaceful Coexistence
Guide to Peaceful Coexistence.tooltip: The Guide to Peaceful Coexistence is a pre-Hardmode tool that combines the effects of the Guide to Critter Companionship and the Guide to Environmental Preservation, preventing player attacks from harming critters and breaking plants when placed within the inventory.

Rubblemaker (Small).name: Rubblemaker (Small)
Rubblemaker (Small).tooltip: The Rubblemaker is a Hardmode tool used to place ambient objects ("rubble") using items from the player's inventory . It is sold by the Goblin Tinkerer during Hardmode for 25 GC .

Closed Void Bag.name: Closed Void Bag
Closed Void Bag.tooltip: The Void Bag is a portable storage item that grants the player access to the Void Vault anywhere. When used, it will summon a temporary portal which lasts for 3 minutes, and pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the portal opens the player's Void Vault inventory. The Void Bag is never consumed and can be used limitlessly.

Artisan Loaf.name: Artisan Loaf
Artisan Loaf.tooltip: The Artisan Loaf is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the range that the player can access crafting stations by 4 tiles in all directions.

TNT Barrel.name: TNT Barrel
TNT Barrel.tooltip: The TNT Barrel is a trap which explodes immediately when hit by virtually any weapon or tool.

Chest Lock.name: Chest Lock
Chest Lock.tooltip: The Chest Lock is a consumable item. Pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on certain types of Chests when holding it will turn the Chest into a locked Chest and consume the Chest Lock.

Rubblemaker (Medium).name: Rubblemaker (Medium)
Rubblemaker (Medium).tooltip: The Rubblemaker is a Hardmode tool used to place ambient objects ("rubble") using items from the player's inventory . It is sold by the Goblin Tinkerer during Hardmode for 25 GC .

Rubblemaker (Large).name: Rubblemaker (Large)
Rubblemaker (Large).tooltip: The Rubblemaker is a Hardmode tool used to place ambient objects ("rubble") using items from the player's inventory . It is sold by the Goblin Tinkerer during Hardmode for 25 GC .

Bundle of Horseshoe Balloons.name: Bundle of Horseshoe Balloons
Bundle of Horseshoe Balloons.tooltip: The Bundle of Horseshoe Balloons is an accessory which combines the functionalities of the Bundle of Balloons and the Lucky Horseshoe.

Spiffo Plush.name: Spiffo Plush
Spiffo Plush.tooltip: The Spiffo Plush is a pet-summoning item that spawns Spiffo to follow the player.

Glow Tulip.name: Glow Tulip
Glow Tulip.tooltip: The Glow Tulip is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Caveling Gardener that follows the player.

Ocram's Razor.name: Ocram's Razor
Ocram's Razor.tooltip: Ocram's Razor is a Hardmode boss-summoning item that summons Mechdusa when used.

Rod of Harmony.name: Rod of Harmony
Rod of Harmony.tooltip: The Rod of Harmony is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord tool.

Advanced Combat Techniques: Volume Two.name: Advanced Combat Techniques: Volume Two
Advanced Combat Techniques: Volume Two.tooltip: Advanced Combat Techniques: Volume Two is a Hardmode permanent booster item that permanently increases the defense of Town NPCs by 6 and attack damage by 20%, similar to the increases after each type of boss is defeated.

Vital Crystal.name: Vital Crystal
Vital Crystal.tooltip: The Vital Crystal is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's health regeneration.

Aegis Fruit.name: Aegis Fruit
Aegis Fruit.tooltip: The Aegis Fruit is a Hardmode permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's defense by 4.

Arcane Crystal.name: Arcane Crystal
Arcane Crystal.tooltip: The Arcane Crystal is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's mana regeneration.

Galaxy Pearl.name: Galaxy Pearl
Galaxy Pearl.tooltip: The Galaxy Pearl is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's luck by 0.03.

Gummy Worm.name: Gummy Worm
Gummy Worm.tooltip: The Gummy Worm is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's fishing power by 3.

Ambrosia.name: Ambrosia
Ambrosia.tooltip: Ambrosia is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's mining, tile, and wall placement speed by 5%.

Peddler's Satchel.name: Peddler's Satchel
Peddler's Satchel.tooltip: The Peddler's Satchel is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the number of items sold by the Traveling Merchant by 1.

Echo Coating.name: Echo Coating
Echo Coating.tooltip: Paint is used to modify the color of objects. Nearly anything can be painted, including blocks , background walls , and furniture , along with non-collectable environment objects like trees , tall grass, flowers, and other ambient growth. Basic paint is purchased from the Painter NPC . Two of the same color can be combined at a Dye Vat to create "deep" color versions, which apply their color more vividly and are required in order to paint certain objects.

Echo Chamber.name: Echo Chamber
Echo Chamber.tooltip: The Echo Chamber is a furniture item. It can be activated and deactivated similarly to a monolith.

Gas Trap.name: Gas Trap
Gas Trap.tooltip: The Gas Trap is a trap item obtained by throwing a Whoopie Cushion into Shimmer.

Aether Monolith.name: Aether Monolith
Aether Monolith.tooltip: Monoliths are furniture items that activate backgrounds and other screen effects normally seen during events or under other special circumstances. When placed, they can be toggled with the ⚷ Open / Activate button or via wire , like other mechanisms , providing their effects in a small area around them. They can also be equipped as vanity accessories , which enables their effect globally for the player, similarly to the Radio Thing .

Shimmer Arrow.name: Shimmer Arrow
Shimmer Arrow.tooltip: The Shimmer Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow that is obtained by throwing a Wooden or Hellfire Arrow into Shimmer.

Aetherium Block.name: Aetherium Block
Aetherium Block.tooltip: Aetherium Blocks are blocks formed when Shimmer comes into contact with any other liquid besides itself.

Faeling.name: Faeling
Faeling.tooltip: The Faeling is a flying critter which naturally spawns in the Aether.

Faeling in a Bottle.name: Faeling in a Bottle
Faeling in a Bottle.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks ). They occupy less room than a chandelier , making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire .

Shimmer Slime Banner.name: Shimmer Slime Banner
Shimmer Slime Banner.tooltip: Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks and platforms . They are dropped by most enemies and a few critters .

Aether Torch.name: Aether Torch
Aether Torch.tooltip: Torches are furniture items that produce light when placed , held, or dropped (via the Throw key), and are crucial at all stages of gameplay as primary light sources . Torches provide light permanently, and are never extinguished. Regular Torches can be found randomly in Chests and Pots , as a bonus drop from slimes , or purchased from the Merchant or Skeleton Merchant for 50 CC each.

Reflective Shades.name: Reflective Shades
Reflective Shades.tooltip: The Reflective Shades are a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Darkness and Stoned debuffs.

Chromatic Cloak.name: Chromatic Cloak
Chromatic Cloak.tooltip: The Chromatic Cloak is a Hardmode accessory which allows for more controlled Shimmering.

Used Gas Trap.name: Used Gas Trap
Used Gas Trap.tooltip: The Gas Trap is a trap item obtained by throwing a Whoopie Cushion into Shimmer . It can also be activated from Chests in No traps and Get fixed boi worlds.

Aether Campfire.name: Aether Campfire
Aether Campfire.tooltip: The Campfire is a placed furniture item that emits light and provides the Cozy Fire buff to players in its vicinity. A Campfire can be turned off by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on the object or by sending it a wire signal, and can be toggled back on again the same way. It is also used to cook a Marshmallow on a Stick .

Shellphone (Home).name: Shellphone (Home)
Shellphone (Home).tooltip: The Shellphone is a post- Skeletron informational item and tool that combines the functions of the Cell Phone , Magic Conch , and Demon Conch . The player can press ⚷ Open / Activate to cycle through four teleport locations: the world's spawn point , the Ocean , the Underworld , and the player's spawn point set via a Bed .

Shellphone (Spawn).name: Shellphone (Spawn)
Shellphone (Spawn).tooltip: The Shellphone is a post- Skeletron informational item and tool that combines the functions of the Cell Phone , Magic Conch , and Demon Conch . The player can press ⚷ Open / Activate to cycle through four teleport locations: the world's spawn point , the Ocean , the Underworld , and the player's spawn point set via a Bed .

Shellphone (Ocean).name: Shellphone (Ocean)
Shellphone (Ocean).tooltip: The Shellphone is a post- Skeletron informational item and tool that combines the functions of the Cell Phone , Magic Conch , and Demon Conch . The player can press ⚷ Open / Activate to cycle through four teleport locations: the world's spawn point , the Ocean , the Underworld , and the player's spawn point set via a Bed .

Shellphone (Underworld).name: Shellphone (Underworld)
Shellphone (Underworld).tooltip: The Shellphone is a post- Skeletron informational item and tool that combines the functions of the Cell Phone , Magic Conch , and Demon Conch . The player can press ⚷ Open / Activate to cycle through four teleport locations: the world's spawn point , the Ocean , the Underworld , and the player's spawn point set via a Bed .

Music Box (Aether).name: Music Box (Aether)
Music Box (Aether).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 GC . When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

Infested Spider Wall.name: Infested Spider Wall
Infested Spider Wall.tooltip: The Spider Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Spider Nests , considered unsafe . It does not drop as an item when destroyed and can only be obtained on Desktop , Console , and Mobile , via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

Bottomless Shimmer Bucket.name: Bottomless Shimmer Bucket
Bottomless Shimmer Bucket.tooltip: Bottomless Buckets are tools that are capable of placing an infinite amount of liquids by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button. There are four different types of Bottomless Buckets, one for each type of liquid: Bottomless Water Bucket , Bottomless Lava Bucket , Bottomless Honey Bucket , and Bottomless Shimmer Bucket .

Cursed Blue Brick Wall.name: Cursed Blue Brick Wall
Cursed Blue Brick Wall.tooltip: Dungeon Brick Walls are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Dungeon , considered unsafe . They drop as items when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting on Desktop , Console , and Mobile . They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.

Treacherous Sandstone Wall.name: Treacherous Sandstone Wall
Treacherous Sandstone Wall.tooltip: The Sandstone Wall , Ebonsandstone Wall , Crimsandstone Wall , and Pearlsandstone Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Desert , considered unsafe . Underground Deserts generate by default the normal Sandstone Sand Wall which may be converted into the respective variant if exposed to the Corruption , Crimson , or Hallow . Converted Sandstone Walls may further spread conversion to other walls; see Biome spread for more information. Unsafe Sandstone Walls do not drop as items when destroyed, and can only be obtained via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.

Treacherous Hardened Sand Wall.name: Treacherous Hardened Sand Wall
Treacherous Hardened Sand Wall.tooltip: The Hardened Sand Wall , Hardened Ebonsand Wall , Hardened Crimsand Wall , and Hardened Pearlsand Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Desert , considered unsafe . Underground Deserts generate by default the normal Hardened Sand Wall which may be converted into the respective variant if exposed to the Corruption , Crimson , or Hallow . Converted Hardened Sand Walls may further spread conversion; see Biome spread for more information. Unsafe Hardened Sand Walls do not drop as items when destroyed, and can only be obtained via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.

Forbidden Lihzahrd Brick Wall.name: Forbidden Lihzahrd Brick Wall
Forbidden Lihzahrd Brick Wall.tooltip: The Lihzahrd Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in the Jungle Temple , considered unsafe . It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

Spelunker Flare.name: Spelunker Flare
Spelunker Flare.tooltip: Flares are a type of ammunition used solely by the Flare Gun . Flares fired from the Flare Gun travel in a slight arc and stick to blocks (similar to Sticky Glowsticks ), but have greater velocity and range. They are waterproof, can be fired into and out of water , and emit low-level, flickering, tinted light that lasts for 10 minutes. They stick to the blocks they impacted and will function underwater. Flares cannot be recovered once they burn out.

Enchanted Moondial.name: Enchanted Moondial
Enchanted Moondial.tooltip: The Enchanted Moondial is a furniture item that can be placed.

Waffle's Iron.name: Waffle's Iron
Waffle's Iron.tooltip: The Waffle's Iron is a Hardmode sword that shoots a waffle projectile once per swing, which is significantly affected by gravity.

Bouncy Boulder.name: Bouncy Boulder
Bouncy Boulder.tooltip: The Bouncy Boulder is a placeable object that begins to roll and bounce when it becomes unsupported.

Life Crystal Boulder.name: Life Crystal Boulder
Life Crystal Boulder.tooltip: The Life Crystal Boulder is a furniture item. It spawns naturally in the Celebrationmk10, No traps, and the Get fixed boi secret world seeds.

Dizzy's Rare Gecko Chester.name: Dizzy's Rare Gecko Chester
Dizzy's Rare Gecko Chester.tooltip: Dizzy's Rare Gecko Chester is a vanity item that has a 1/14 (7.14%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops.

Raynebro's Hoodie.name: Raynebro's Hoodie
Raynebro's Hoodie.tooltip: Raynebro's set is a vanity set consisting of Raynebro's Hood , Raynebro's Hoodie , and Raynebro's Pants . It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 3 GC (set) .

Raynebro's Pants.name: Raynebro's Pants
Raynebro's Pants.tooltip: Raynebro's set is a vanity set consisting of Raynebro's Hood , Raynebro's Hoodie , and Raynebro's Pants . It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 3 GC (set) .

Cheesy Pizza Poster.name: Cheesy Pizza Poster
Cheesy Pizza Poster.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls . Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria -related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members ( see Trivia below ) . (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions , the Magic Lantern , Spelunker Glowsticks , and Spelunker Flares .

Raynebro's Hood.name: Raynebro's Hood
Raynebro's Hood.tooltip: Raynebro's set is a vanity set consisting of Raynebro's Hood , Raynebro's Hoodie , and Raynebro's Pants . It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 3 GC (set) .

Uncumbering Stone.name: Uncumbering Stone
Uncumbering Stone.tooltip: The Encumbering Stone is a pre-Hardmode tool that prevents item pickup while inside the player's inventory . While in the inventory, the Encumbering Stone will prevent the pickup of any items, even if the player already has a stackable item in their inventory. The Encumbering Stone will also prevent items from being added to the Void Bag .

Yellow Solution.name: Yellow Solution
Yellow Solution.tooltip: Solutions are a type of ammunition used solely by the Clentaminator and Terraformer . Each solution will convert certain blocks and walls to other blocks and walls, creating and/or destroying different biomes in the process. There are 8 different solutions. 7 of them are sold by the Steampunker , who sells different solutions based on certain conditions, and one is sold by the Truffle , who always sells it.

Guide to Critter Companionship (Inactive.name: Guide to Critter Companionship (Inactive)
Guide to Critter Companionship (Inactive.tooltip: The Guide to Critter Companionship is a pre-Hardmode tool that prevents the player's attacks from harming critters while inside their inventory . It can be purchased from the Zoologist for 5 GC .

Guide to Environmental Preservation (Ina.name: Guide to Environmental Preservation (Inactive)
Guide to Environmental Preservation (Ina.tooltip: The Guide to Environmental Preservation is a pre-Hardmode tool that prevents the player's attacks from breaking plants while inside their inventory . It can be purchased from the Dryad for 5 GC .

Guide to Peaceful Coexistence (Inactive).name: Guide to Peaceful Coexistence (Inactive)
Guide to Peaceful Coexistence (Inactive).tooltip: The Guide to Peaceful Coexistence is a pre-Hardmode tool that combines the effects of the Guide to Critter Companionship and the Guide to Environmental Preservation , preventing player attacks from harming critters and breaking plants when placed within the inventory .
